title: Welded Asteroids
description: The closed-loop stigmergic field itself, living on the quotient surfaces of the topology game: physarum agents, trail and agent-deposited momentum all obey the surface's gluing rule. Six tour levels bind surface + parameter presets + a beta_1 target; 18 declared sliders drive the physarum; the asteroids game survives as a hidden Easter egg (X when beta_1 >= 42). v2.0.1: seam crossings now transform position AND heading together (topo-asteroids flipP protocol — fixes agents stranding at the Klein/projective seams); sim square letterboxed to true 1:1 (fixes stretched height map). v2.1.0: the real fix for the Klein seam-wall — three compounding defects. (1) foldRead/momRead/uvOf mirrored the WRONG axis (topo.y.flip='x' names the axis that mirrors; the code mirrored the other one), so agent sensing disagreed with deposits. (2) Diffusion sampled neighbors with plain torus wrap; on a mirrored identification the flux at the seam never cancels and mass was slowly pumped into the two seam rows — the minutes-scale accumulator. Now neighbor sampling honors the gluing rule (mirrored cell across a mirrored seam) for trail AND momentum, with the vector's mirrored component sign-flipping. (3) Sense samples crossing a mirrored seam have swapped left/right meaning relative to the agent's square frame; the turn rule now swaps L/R when the front and a flank read different fold images — near-seam agents no longer turn back into the seam. Also fixed: wrapPos wrap-count for negative coordinates (floor division) and double-flip when a y-fold pushed x out of range. Verified: 150s Klein soak — no seam wall, no edge pinning; torus/projective/Mobius 45s soaks all stable.

cogdoc.claim: The closed-loop stigmergic field's native domain is a quotient surface: agent writes and reads both obey the surface's gluing rule (mirrored re-entry on Klein/projective/Mobius, walls on the strip), so the simulation itself provides the levels and the beta_1 readout is measured on the surface the structures actually live on.
